title: Kernel of the ab–ca vote correlation
statement:
Fix a natural number $n$ and consider profiles $p$ of $n$ voters, each of whom reports one of the six strict orderings of the three alternatives $a, b, c$; there are $6^n$ such profiles. For a profile $p$, let $x^{ab}(p) \in \{0,1\}^n$ be the vector recording each voter's preference in the $a$-vs-$b$ comparison, and $x^{ca}(p) \in \{0,1\}^n$ the vector recording each voter's preference in the $c$-vs-$a$ comparison. Then for any two subsets $S, T \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, the averaged product of the corresponding Walsh–Fourier characters satisfies
\[
  \left(\tfrac{1}{6}\right)^{\!n} \sum_{p} \chi_S\bigl(x^{ab}(p)\bigr)\,\chi_T\bigl(x^{ca}(p)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \begin{cases} \left(-\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{|S|} & \text{if } S = T,\\[2pt] 0 & \text{if } S \neq T, \end{cases}
\]
where the sum ranges over all $6^n$ profiles.
hypotheses_covered: S and T are subsets (finite sets) of the index set {1,...,n}
n is a natural number and the sum is over all 6^n profiles p : Fin n → Fin 6
